description: Per-file content provenance for the W3-B skills: unslop, bro, technical-writing, no-comments (including references/comment-sicko.md), in-your-own-words, ketchup and sharpen. Owned by the W3-B writer; see test/skill-content.test.ts for the rules. teach and poteto-help moved to skills/merged (merged.json).

files.explanation: Byte-identical copy of the pinned pi-mimir file, which also equals the Cursor file. Seven lines by design; it needs no adaptation.

Adapted from the pinned pi-mimir file. Mimir step 1 called a named comment-sicko role through agent; pstack registers no roles (plan 09 and user decision D2), so a new Comment Sicko section launches it as a deliberate bare delegate with one schema-valid subagent example: name, task scope, systemPrompt holding the full text of references/comment-sicko.md read verbatim, tools read, bash, edit (D1: it edits comments only), model task:review or an exact provider/model-id, thinking, fork false and no worktree. If the prompt file is missing or filtered the skill stops and never launches a bare child without it. Step 1 points at that call. Step 2 marks /skill:how and /skill:why planned W4 with the interim rule (trace it yourself, say the skills were unavailable; ambiguous keeps follow the skill's own delete rule). Step 3 marks /skill:architect planned W4 and says to sketch two or three shapes yourself and record architect skipped: planned W4. Step 4 keeps the upstream principle sentence; its cross-batch planned W3 marker was retired at the W3 reconcile. Step 6 also reports that the delegate was bare. Cursor's Task/subagent_type wording is not used. Parent edit after the real-child gate: states that fork: false is required because the host delivers a bare systemPrompt only to standalone children, as a role block in the first message. W4 reconcile: the how/why and architect planned W4 markers and their interim fallbacks are retired now that those skills ship, restoring the upstream step 2 and 3 wording.

Body of the pinned pi-mimir comment-sicko role file, shipped as the bare-delegate prompt that no-comments passes as systemPrompt (user decision D2). The frontmatter is dropped because this is a prompt, not a role. Its read-only reviewer description, which contradicted a body that deletes comments, is reworded as an opening paragraph: it deletes comments and suppressions, edits comments only and never application code, and reports touched files and deletion counts (D1). The persona line is kept verbatim. The /skill:how and /skill:why line is marked planned W4 with the interim rule (read the symbol, callers and history itself and report the skills unavailable). The dropped spawning: false and the tools change become one paragraph: bash is for reading and history, deletions go through the edit tool, and it does not commit, push or launch subagents. 'Report only.' becomes 'My last message is the report and nothing else.' so it no longer reads as read-only. W4 reconcile: the how/why planned W4 marker and interim fallback are retired; the line now says the delegate is a leaf and takes their single-pass path, tracing the symbol itself and launching nothing (fan-out section 1, gate G7).

Pinned pi-mimir file (mimir is primary because it adds the review checklist that Cursor lacks and already uses Pi's /skill:technical-writing syntax), unchanged except for one added paragraph. #37 decision 6: an 'Audience: humans' paragraph after the intro says this skill governs prose for human readers, that instructions an agent reads and acts on (a skill, AGENTS.md, a doc an agent reaches through a pointer) follow the writing-for-agents skill (../../mattpocock/writing-for-agents/SKILL.md), and that where they conflict the reader decides: in a document for humans this skill wins; in a document for agents writing-for-agents wins, so its leading words stay even where this skill skips metaphors.
